key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 was elevated in both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), while its ratio to neurofilament light chain (NfL) better distinguished the two.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that elevated p-tau217 should be interpreted in disease context rather than assumed to indicate AD alone.
method: Studied 551 participants across 10 diagnostic groups, including 45 amyloid-PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls.
Measured baseline plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP.
Compared biomarker profiles and evaluated discrimination using ROC-AUC analyses.
evidence_signal: The p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD with an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.97), versus 0.65 (0.52–0.76) for p-tau217 alone.
watch_item: The supplied abstract is truncated and concerns neurodegenerative biomarkers—not AI cancer drug discovery; its cross-sectional discrimination findings do not establish clinical diagnostic utility.
paper_title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
